<subject>Electronic Transactions Agreement - revised</subject>
<body>
As you know, the ETA must accommodate [ORG_1] one-to-many with [COMPANY] and [ORG_4] one-to-many with [COMPANY]. We also require a standalone [ORG_1] GTC one-to-many with [COMPANY] and separate [ORG_4] GTC one-to-many with [COMPANY]. Additionally, a single [ORG_2] application must support [ORG_3], both one-to-many.

Once these drafts are finalized, I’d like to review them promptly.

Thanks.

Lee Mills  
Associate  
Maple & Crown Telecom Inc.  
Phone: (403) 555-0287  
Email: lee.mills@maplecrown.ca  
</body>
<quoted>
-----Original Message-----
From: Jordan Pierce <jordan.pierce@maplecrown.ca>
Sent: Tuesday, 9 July 2024 8:33 PM
To: Lee Mills <lee.mills@maplecrown.ca>; Nicholas Porter <nicholas.porter@maplecrown.ca>; John Cummings <john.cummings@maplecrown.ca>; Bradley Miller <bradley.miller@maplecrown.ca>; Douglas Dixon <douglas.dixon@maplecrown.ca>; Harry M Collins <harry.collins@maplecrown.ca>; Sandra Wood <sandra.wood@maplecrown.ca>
Subject: Electronic Transactions Agreement - revised

Attached is a revised version of the ETA removing the distinction between transactions on [ORG_4] and transactions on [ORG_1]. If [COMPANY] is the sole party authorized to post services on [ORG_4], the prior "many-to-many" matching rules are no longer necessary. However, we’ll need a new set of GTCs for transactions [COMPANY] executes on [ORG_4], as the services traded there won’t align with [COMPANY]'s standard GTC framework.
